title: The Fourteen Months in Which Sendy Wound Down
dek: From mid-2022 the Nairobi delivery company cut staff, paused a product and left Nigeria; in 2023 a funding round fell apart and it went into administration.

story.founder: Meshack Alloys, Evanson Biwott, Don Okoth, Malaika Judd
story.event: Closing a Nairobi delivery company after a funding round and a sale fell through
story.summary: Sendy, a Nairobi delivery company founded in 2015 by Meshack Alloys, Evanson Biwott, Don Okoth and Malaika Judd, cut staff in July and October 2022, paused its Sendy Supply service and left Nigeria in February 2023. After a key investor reportedly withdrew from a new round, it shut its operations in August 2023 and sought a buyer; when no sale came, Peter Kahi of PKF Consulting was appointed administrator of its companies from 20 September 2023.
paragraphs: On 8 August 2023 Meshack Alloys confirmed to TechCrunch that Sendy, the Nairobi delivery company he had co-founded in 2015 with Evanson Biwott, Don Okoth and Malaika Judd, was in the middle of an acquisition process. The same report said Sendy was shutting its operations and that more than 200 employees would be affected. The company matched businesses with motorbike riders, vans and trucks, and in 2020 it had raised about $20 million in a round led by Atlantica Ventures and Toyota Tsusho.

The end had come in steps. Since 2021 Sendy had been trying to raise $100 million to expand across Africa, and it got only a fraction. In July 2022 it cut a tenth of its staff, which Alloys tied to "current realities impacting tech companies globally". In October it paused Sendy Supply, a service that let shopkeepers buy stock from several suppliers; Alloys said the change affected 20 percent of the workforce, and the company later said every affected employee had been paid their terminal benefits. MOL PLUS, the venture arm of a Japanese shipping firm, invested late that year. In February 2023 Sendy left Nigeria.

Then a new round fell apart. Sendy had been valued at more than $80 million in late 2022, and, according to people familiar with the company who spoke to TechCrunch, it was negotiating at $40 million to $60 million when a key investor withdrew, leaving it short of money, salaries included, for two to three months. It talked to other firms, among them Trella, Sabi and Wasoko, about buying its technology and fulfilment business. "So yes, Sendy is being acquired," Alloys said, and promised a joint statement in about two weeks.

No sale was announced. With effect from 20 September 2023, Peter Kahi of PKF Consulting was appointed administrator of four Sendy companies, a formal insolvency process that took day-to-day control away from the directors; Business Daily reported that the sale had fallen through. Anyone Sendy owed was asked to file a claim by 19 October. Disclosed investment totalled $26.5 million, or $29 million by another count. In late 2025 Alloys launched tabb, a company building trade credit for small businesses.

quote.text: But the ship is sinking—what then have I to do? I do the only thing that I can, not to be drowned full of fear, nor screaming nor blaming God, but knowing that what has been produced must also perish
quote.locator: Discourses, Book II, Chapter 5, "How magnanimity is consistent with care"
quote.source_title: A Selection from the Discourses of Epictetus with the Encheiridion, tr. George Long, Project Gutenberg eBook #10661
quote.connection: Epictetus asks for care in what we can choose and composure when the ship goes down anyway. Over fourteen months Sendy's founders cut, paused, withdrew from a market and looked for a buyer. Some of what decided the end, such as an investor's withdrawal, lay outside their hands.

reflection: Companies rarely end in a single day. Sendy's end ran through more than a year of smaller decisions, each one defensible on its own, and through one decision taken by someone else. Reading it, you can see how much of the outcome sat outside the founders' hands, and how much still rested with them: what departing staff were paid, and whether the people owed money had a proper way to claim it.
You cannot choose the weather your work will meet. You can keep what you owe other people written down and current, so that if a storm does come, that part of the care is already done.
invitation: Pick one promise you have made to someone, whether money, a piece of work or a reply, that is not yet written down anywhere. Write it where you will see it next week, and leave the rest for today.

research_notes: Founders: the slate listed 'Evans Ochieng'; TechCrunch and TechMoran both name the fourth co-founder as Evanson Biwott, so the story uses that. Founding year: 2015 (TechCrunch, TechMoran, Techweez 2026) versus 2014 (Daba Finance); the story uses 2015. Total funding: $26.5 million disclosed (TechCrunch) versus $29 million (Business Daily, HapaKenya); both are given without choosing. October 2022 cut: Alloys said 20 percent (HapaKenya), TechCrunch counted 54 employees, and TechMoran's own headline link says 10 percent; the story gives Alloys's 20 percent. The $100 million target: Business Daily says sought since 2021; TechCrunch says 'last year' in an August 2023 article but links a 2021 report; the story says since 2021. The failed round, the valuations ($80 million-plus, then $40-60 million) and two to three months short of salary money come only from TechCrunch's unnamed sources and are attributed to them; Techpoint (9 August 2023) reports the same investor withdrawal but is blocked for the verifier and is not cited. No source records whether the promised joint statement was ever issued; the story says only that no sale was announced, and Business Daily reports the sale fell through. Business Daily says the High Court appointed the administrator, while the published notice quoted by Techweez says only that he was appointed; the story does not say by whom. Staff affected: TechCrunch's 'over 200 employees' is given as the company's position at closure; no source reports final payments to staff at closure, and the statement about terminal benefits refers to the 2022 layoffs, as the story says. No founder account of the decision itself was found (TechCabal, which reported in depth, blocks automated requests), so the story uses only Alloys's public statements and states no feelings or motives. Causes are not assigned beyond the reported investor withdrawal and Alloys's own words. The Epictetus passage is Discourses II.5 in Long's translation (the Gutenberg selection prints it under the chapter title without a number).
